reproResult: Followed the four repro steps at 16ceb3a54 in my own worktree (dev instance app :18014 / server :26014 / data dir ~/.bb-dev/projects-bb-.claude-worktrees-wf_6b6686dc-4c2-7-34ff9ca60a27). Step 1 works. Step 2 as written fails with 'Permission denied' (1131-seed.sh is -rw-rw-r--); with `bash 1131-seed.sh` it built the identical fixture deterministically (704,206 events, 1,571,041,280-byte bb.db, giant thread thr_v67duphyr7 = 44,004 events / 70,702,989 bytes) in 33 s. Step 4 (1131-cold-timeline.sh, run twice; outputs in 1131/verify/cold-timeline-verify-run{1,2}.out): cold timeline build 322 ms / 296 ms, server read_bytes delta 99,295,232 / 99,713,024 for a 329,482-byte response, /health probe stalled 320 ms / 295 ms, warm second request 3-4 ms -- matches the report's numbers closely even at load avg 68. Profiler (1131/verify/profile-verify-*.out): cold totalMs 411, diskReadBytes 99,966,976, majorPageFaults 918, top statements 73,004 KiB (todo snapshot) and 20,256 KiB (parent-tool-call scan); warm parent scan 73 ms CPU with 0 bytes -- identical to the report. Unit test passes 3/3 with ratio 29.0x. Cold thread-list control: 62 ms, 0 disk bytes, 3,287 threads. Truncation stats reproduced exactly (56,166 outputs, 0 > 32 KB, 51,453 > 4 KB, 0 truncated). All 17 permalinked excerpts exist at the cited lines; origin/main (5 commits ahead) does not touch these two queries, so not fixed. Discrepancy: on my first run the /health probe also recorded 27.98 s and 22.49 s stalls that are NOT the timeline: dev.log shows the destroyed-environment prune sweep `delete from environments where id in (1543 ids)` took 26,776 ms (SET NULL over ~297k seeded event rows) and the output-truncation sweep UPDATE took 0.1-4.7 s per tick ('Event loop stalled' 11 s), none of which the report mentions.

findings.problem: The reader's observed output can differ materially from the report's 'Actual': right after (re)starting the server on the freshly seeded db, background sweeps block the loop for tens of seconds and show up in the /health probe, and the report neither warns about this nor explains it. It also means the report missed additional multi-second synchronous DB work on the same seeded db (partly a seed artifact: 1,543 destroyed environments whose deletion SET-NULLs ~297k event rows).
findings.evidence: 1131/verify/cold-timeline-verify-run1.out: '/health probe slowest: 14:12:42.471 ttfb=27.976532s, 14:13:15.246 ttfb=22.491556s' while the timeline itself was 0.32 s. dev.log 14:13:09: 'Slow DB query durationMs 26776.4 delete from "environments" where id in (1543 ?)' (started 14:12:42, matching the stall); 14:13:40 'UPDATE events SET data = json_set(...) durationMs 3969.1'; 14:13:46 'Event loop stalled maxDelayMs 11047.8 slowestWork sweep:completed-event-output-truncation 6015.5'. Second run (after sweeps settled) matched the report: 296 ms build, 295 ms health stall.
findings.fix: In the repro, tell the reader to wait until startup sweeps settle (or check dev.log for 'Slow DB query'/'Event loop stalled') before running the script, and state that stalls at other timestamps are sweeps, not the timeline. Add a short note (Deeper issue or Appendix) that the environment-prune SET NULL and the truncation-sweep UPDATE are also synchronous multi-second writes on this database shape.

findings.problem: 1131-seed.sh is not executable, so the command exactly as written fails.
findings.evidence: ls: -rw-rw-r-- 1131-seed.sh (the other .sh files are 755); running `1131/repro/1131-seed.sh` -> '/bin/bash: Permission denied'. Works with `bash 1131/repro/1131-seed.sh`.
findings.fix: chmod +x the script or write the step as `bash 1131/repro/1131-seed.sh`. Also state that the 1131/repro/ paths are relative to /tmp/bb-reports/issues/ and that the seed script patches packages/scripts/src/lib/seed-perf-fixture.ts and the profile script leaves apps/server/issue-1131-profile.ts in the worktree.

findings.section: Claims vs findings / Control: thread list
findings.problem: The thread-list control is labelled 'cold' but its own artifact shows the pages were already cached: posix_fadvise DONTNEED cannot evict pages the just-restarted server touched during startup, so the 52 ms figure is effectively warm. The 'fixed' status still holds via #1204 and the reporter's 0.36.1 confirmation, but the local number overstates the evidence.
findings.evidence: Report artifact 1131-cold-thread-list.out: 'server io before: read_bytes: 0 / after: read_bytes: 8192' for a 3.17 MB response; my run: 569344 -> 569344 (0 bytes). My cold-threads-true.sh (evict, then start server, then first request): server startup alone read 27,205,632 bytes and the first GET /threads read 0 additional bytes at 53 ms.
findings.fix: Relabel as 'first request after restart (threads pages already faulted in by startup)' or measure the query directly in a standalone process after eviction, as the profiler does for the timeline.

findings.problem: 'Make the todo-snapshot lookup index-only' is inaccurate: the proposed partial index on (thread_id, sequence) is not covering; the helper still fetches `data` for every matching row, which the report's own experiment shows (28 MB still read for 520 rows).
findings.evidence: 1131-todo-index-experiment.sql selects `id, data` via events_todo_snapshot_idx; 1131-profile-todo-index-fix-cold.out: '28356 KiB 45 ms x 1 SELECT ... FROM events INDEXED BY events_todo_snapshot_idx'.
findings.fix: Say the partial index limits row visits to the todo/task rows (520 instead of all 2,524 tool-call rows) rather than 'index-only'.
